[[Mother (title)|Mother]] '''Aniseya''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|female]] who lived during the [[High Republic Era]]. She led an [[Exile of Aniseya's coven|exiled]] [[Brendok coven|coven]] of [[witch]]es and eventually settled the group on the [[planet]] [[Brendok]] after they had suffered persecution for some [[time]]. Around [[156 BBY]], Mother Aniseya created the [[twin]] [[Youngling|children]] [[Mae-ho Aniseya|Mae-ho]] and [[Verosha Aniseya]], who were then carried until their [[Reproduction|birth]] by Mother [[Koril]]. Mother Aniseya and Koril raised the sisters together as their [[Parent|mothers]], though the pair often disagreed on how to raise the twins.

In [[148 BBY]], Aniseya hosted [[Rite of Ascension]] ceremony for her daughters to become witches. When several visiting [[Jedi]] [[Mission to Brendok|interrupted]], and Mother Aniseya agreed to let the pair be tested after [[Jedi Master]] [[Indara]] insisted. Not long after, Aniseya [[Death|perished]] when she attempted to forestall further conflict during a confrontation with Master [[Sol]] and the [[Padawan]] [[Torbin]] where the Jedi questioned her about the nature behind her daughters' birth. Triggering the beginnings of a transformation within both herself and Mae-ho, Aniseya was killed by Sol, who mistook her efforts as an attack against him and struck out with his [[lightsaber]], mortally wounding the witch, who explained with her dying breaths that she had been intending to allow Verosha to leave and join the Jedi Order.

Her death having spurred the following battle between the Brendok coven and the Jedi, which resulted in the deaths of most of the witches. Verosha and Mae-ho survived, with the former becoming Sol's Padawan and the latter becoming a [[Sith assassin]] under a [[Sith]] known as "[[the Stranger]]," with both grieving their mother's death for [[Standard year|years]] afterward. Verosha's inability to let go of her feelings of loss for her mother eventually resulted in her agreeing to train under the Stranger following Mae-ho's departure from the Sith's tutelage.

==Biography==
===Leader of an exiled coven===
[[File:Destiny-TheAcolyte-Thumbnail.png|thumb|right|300px|Mother Aniseya in the Brendok fortress]]
[[Mother (title)|Mother]] Aniseya was a [[Gender|female]] [[human]] who lived during the [[High Republic Era]].<ref name="Destiny" /> She<ref name="Cast" /> led a [[Brendok coven|coven]] of [[witch]]es that eventually got [[Exile of Aniseya's coven|exiled]]. During their exile, the coven was persecuted and could not perform their usual ceremonies, such as the [[Rite of Ascension]]. Aniseya eventually settled the witches in a [[Brendok fortress|fortress]] on the [[planet]] [[Brendok]], with the leader insisting to a fellow witch—Mother [[Koril]]—that the world would be safe. When Aniseya [[Reproduction|created]] [[Mae-ho Aniseya|Mae-ho]] and [[Verosha Aniseya]]<ref name="Destiny" /> with the power of a [[vergence]]<ref name="In231">{{InsiderCite|231|A Certain Point of View (department)}}</ref> around [[156 BBY]],<ref name="TwinsBirth">The events of ''[[Star Wars: The Acolyte]]'' take place in [[132 BBY]] per the reasoning [[:Template:TheAcolyteDate|here]]. "[[Lost / Found]]" states that [[Mae-ho Aniseya|Mae-ho]] and [[Verosha Aniseya]] were eight [[Standard year|years]] old when separated. As "[[Destiny (The Acolyte)|Destiny]]" dates itself to sixteen years prior to the series' main events, equating to [[148 BBY]]. The episode also depicts their separation, meaning the pair must have been [[Reproduction|created]] by Aniseya around [[156 BBY]].</ref> Koril carried them in her womb. After their birth, the women both became the [[twin]]s' [[Parent|mothers]]. Though Mother Aniseya often adopted a more relaxed parenting style, in contrast, Koril's fierce protectiveness of the twins<ref name="Destiny" /> made her a comparatively stern and intimidating caretaker.<ref name="Databank-Koril">{{Databank|mother-koril|Mother Koril}}</ref>

When Aniseya and Koril disagreed in parenting matters, the latter deferred to the twins' other mother due to the former being the coven's leader.<ref name="Destiny" /> By [[148 BBY]],<ref name="Date" /> Aniseya had a set of advisors that helped her make decisions, and some had varying levels of authority. Around this [[time]], Verosha began sneaking outside the fortress to explore, which was against the coven's rules for the twins. Mother Aniseya felt that her daughter's rebelliousness was natural for a child, though Koril sharply disagreed and often reprimanded Verosha—and sometimes Mae-ho—for sneaking out. During their childhood, Mother Aniseya trained her daughters how to use [[The Force|the Thread]]—also known as the Force—to train them to become witches.<ref name="Destiny" />

===Training with the Thread===
In 148 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]],<ref name="Date" /> several [[Jedi]]—[[Jedi Master]]s [[Indara]] and [[Kelnacca]], the [[Jedi Knight]] [[Sol]], and the [[Padawan]] [[Torbin]] visited Brendok on a [[Mission to Brendok|mission]], soon discovering the witches after having initially assumed the planet was uninhabited. One [[Standard day|day]], Koril brought the pair's daughters back to the fortress after finding them wandering Brendok's forests. Though Koril did not want to allow the girls to indulge in [[spice cream]]s, Aniseya disagreed, insisting her girls must have treats. The latter mother sent the pair away to prepare for their training session, while Koril deferred to the woman's authority.<ref name="Destiny" />

[[File:KorilAniseyaFortress-Destiny.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Mother Aniseya and Koril conversed about their daughters leaving the fortress while there were Jedi visiting Brendok.]]
Afterward, Mother Aniseya and Koril conversed about their daughters having left the fortress again, as well as the visiting Jedi on Brendok and their [[Polan GX-8|ship's]] location. When the coven leader encouraged the Zabrak to speak freely, Koril indicated her displeasure with the other mother's lenient parenting style but acknowledged that she deferred to the former's judgement due to her authority in the coven. Mother Aniseya expressed that she felt the fortress would keep them safe, though Koril countered that it would not remain so if Verosha continued to leave its safety.<ref name="Destiny" />

In the [[Fortress common room|fortress's common room]], Aniseya then hosted a training session to teach Mae-ho and Verosha how to wield the Thread. She explained what she was doing as she [[Telekinesis|floated]] a [[fruit]] through the [[Atmosphere|air]] and fought off the attacks of one, and then later two witches. However, the twins began squabbling with each other and stopped paying attention to their mother. The coven leader threw both to the ground using the Thread, warning them that their enemies would not give warning before striking. When Mae-ho successfully blocked one of Mother Aniseya's attacks, Verosha hid behind her sister, causing Koril to scold her for not doing better. When a noise sounded in the training room, Koril exchanged a glance with Mother Aniseya and got up to investigate, intently surveying a nearby corridor leading to the coven's electricity generator.<ref name="Destiny" />

===Rite of Ascension===
The coven's witches donned<ref name="Destiny" /> ceremonial purple robes<ref name="Destiny AD" /> and gathered in the [[Rite of Ascension courtyard|fortress's courtyard]] for Mae-ho and Verosha Aniseya's Rite of Ascension ceremony to become witches, with Mother Aniseya putting on an elaborate version of the ones worn by her coven members. The gathered witches parted and let Mother Aniseya move through them, with Koril stepping aside to let the former take the lead position. After Mother Aniseya proclaimed the significance of the ceremony—which they had not performed since before the group's exile—and enumerated on the suffering their group had endured, until now, in which they could rejoice in the gift of life.<ref name="Destiny" />

[[File:AniseyaIndara-Destiny.png|thumb|right|300px|Indara and Mother Aniseya argued on Brendok when the Jedi interrupted the witches' Rite of Ascension.]]
After Mae-ho vowed to keep the coven's secrets, even after its leader's [[death]], Mother Aniseya completed a ritual that left a white, spiraling mark on the girl's forehead. Though Verosha made the same vow, albeit more reluctantly, two witches rushed into the courtyard and informed the leader that the Jedi were coming to their location before she could complete the second Rite of Ascension. At their leader's command, the witches quickly crowded around the children to hide them, with Aniseya making her way to the front and telling her coven to put down their drawn weapons. Indara introduced her colleagues by name to the witches, insisting to the skeptical women that the Jedi did not mean to intrude or cause harm, having thought the world was uninhabited. However, Mother Aniseya mocked these claims and reminded the Jedi that they were carrying weapons. The witches also rebuffed the Jedi's claim that children were present on Brendok, offended at the visitors breaching their sacred inner circle.<ref name="Destiny" />

After Osha caught Indara's [[eye]], the Jedi Master encouraged the child to come out of the crowd of witches, disappointing Aniseya. Mother Aniseya agreed to Indara's inquiry of meeting Mae as well, informing her that the children had no father. When Sol proposed to Osha that she be tested as a Jedi, the child implored her mother for permission. However, Mother Aniseya used a [[Force power|Thread ability]] to incapacitate Torbin, threatening Indara that they needed to leave or she would not undo the effects. Indara insisted that she could not deny the Jedi's right to test potential Padawans, prompting the leader to reluctantly agree to allow the twins to be brought to the Jedi's camp the following [[Standard day|day]]. The Jedi Master thanked them for cooperating, exiting the courtyard with her colleagues.<ref name="Destiny" />

===Testing and fire===
[[File:KorilAniseyaArgument-Destiny.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Aniseya and Koril argued over whether to allow the Jedi to test their daughters.]]
In a meeting of adult witches afterward, Koril Zabrak proposed killing the visiting Jedi, other witches disagreed, as the [[Galactic Republic|Republic]] would be angered if any Jedi blood was spilled. However, Mother Aniseya pointed out that it was her decision to make, and also reminded the Zabrak that she had created the twins. Koril countered that she had carried the twins and did not want to lose them to "deranged monks." The elder witch [[Naasa]], however, offered her advice that the two children would be forcibly taken away if they passed the test, with the leader considered.<ref name="Destiny" />

[[File:AniseyaKorilAfterTesting-Destiny.png|thumb|right|300px|Aniseya and Koril spoke with their daughters after their Jedi testing.]]
The following day, the girls were set to tested by the Jedi and sat with Mother Aniseya beforehand. The woman encouraged them to lie, though Verosha was hesitant. The coven leader told her that what she wanted may change, even if she wished to be a Jedi now, that may not always be the case, and that she and her sister were powerful, special girls. Following this, Mae-ho failed the test by lying, Verosha opted to tell the truth and passed the test. Mother Aniseya and Koril sat with the other witches in the coven's common room afterward, as the girls explained what happened. When Mae-ho began to tussle with her sister for their differing viewpoints, Koril dragged the child away forcibly to go on a walk at Mother Aniseya's suggestion. When Verosha continued to insist she had not wanted to lie and did want to be a Jedi, her mother accepted her answer and promised to consider her wishes as the witches discussed, but indicated such things were rarely simple.<ref name="Destiny" />

After, Verosha began packing to leave with the Jedi.<ref name="Destiny" /> However, Sol and Torbin soon arrived, intending to take the twins due to a belief that they were a [[vergence]] in the Force. Aniseya, alongside Koril, confronted the Jedi once again for trespassing. Meanwhile, Mae-ho had started a fire in an attempt to prevent her sister's departure. Shortly thereafter, Mae-ho arrived to warn her mother, only for Koril to suddenly attack Torbin. In an attempt to prevent violence, Aniseya began to act, dissipating into a black smoke and triggering a similar transformation for Mae-ho. Before she could fully dissipate, however, Sol stabbed her with his lightsaber. Sol grabbed Aniseya, who confessed that she was going to let Verosha leave. Just after, she died. The witches then tried to shoot and mind-control the Jedi to death, but their revenge efforts were unsuccessful.<ref name="Choice">{{Acolyte|Choice}}</ref>

After Verosha was later saved from the fire by Sol, the girl saw Mother Aniseya's body dead on the floor as they fled, traumatizing her.<ref name="Destiny" /> Afterward, Verosha became Sol's Padawan, though continued to mourn her mothers' deaths for years after their passing and harbored resentment toward Mae-ho for destroying their family, having been told that the coven had perished as a result of the fire lit by her twin sister. Eventually, Verosha left the Jedi<ref name="LostFound">{{Acolyte|Lost / Found}}</ref> around [[138 BBY]] and by [[132 BBY]],<ref name="Date-LF">{{TheAcolyteDate}} "[[Lost / Found]]" establishes that [[Verosha Aniseya]] left the [[Jedi Order]] six years before its events, equating to around [[138 BBY]], as the episode's events take place in [[132 BBY]].</ref> she still mourned the loss of her family.<ref name="LostFound" /> Mae-ho, who the Jedi believed to have perished that night as well, eventually became apprenticed<ref name="Acolyte 2">{{Acolyte|Revenge / Justice}}</ref> to a mysterious [[Sith Lord]] calling himself "[[the Stranger]]"<ref name="EW">{{WebCite|url=https://ew.com/the-acolyte-episode-5-bloodbath-villain-reveal-cover-story-exclusive-8665633|text=Seeing red: Inside The Acolyte's shocking bloodbath and big villain reveal|author=Ross, Dalton|date=2024-06-26|archivedate=20240626175005}}</ref>, who eventually tasked her with [[Mae's quest|killing]] the four Jedi stationed on [[Brendok]] at the time of her mothers' deaths.<ref name="Day">{{Acolyte|Day (episode)}}</ref> Many years after her death, Mother Aniseya was regarded by Sol as having been an unusually strong manipulator of the Force.<ref name="Destiny AD" />

==Personality and traits==
[[File:WomenoftheGalaxy-MotherAniseya.png|thumb|left|300px|Mother Aniseya of Brendok]]
Aniseya and Koril shared a close, companionable bond with each other, which was furthered by the matriarchal culture of their community.<ref name="Newsnet">{{WebCite|url=https://www.starwarsnewsnet.com/2024/06/leslye-headland-on-queerness-in-the-acolyte-the-witch-coven-and-more.html|text=Leslye Headland on Queerness in 'The Acolyte', the Witch Coven, and More|author=[https://www.starwarsnewsnet.com/author/sydney-watsek Sydney Sumpter]|date=2024-06-21|archivedate=20240621201005}}</ref> The pair shared several moments of gently emotionally comforting each other<ref name="Destiny AD" /> and Mother Aniseya encouraged the Zabrak to voice her opinions and concerns to her. However, the coven leader was also willing to exercise her authority and directly defy Koril's adamant wish for the Jedi not to test the pair's daughters, insisting it was her decision alone as their leader. Additionally, she was proud of her prowess at using the Thread, not bothered by how her abilities were dark. The witch thought that the continuation of her witch coven was of great importance.<ref name="Destiny" />

Aniseya was willing to let Osha follow her wish and become a Jedi, but never told anyone until she lay dying after a Jedi mistook her transformation into a mist form as an attack. Just before this incident, she tried to restrain Koril and the rest of her coven and the Jedi from coming to blows.<ref name="Choice" /> Aniseya had [[Color|brown]] eyes and brown skin with white [[tattoo]]s. The coven leader had black [[hair]] with brown highlights, which she styled in a set of elaborate [[braid]]s.<ref name="Destiny" /> Mother Aniseya stood 1.75 [[meter]]s tall.<ref name="Databank-Aniseya" />

==Powers and abilities==
Aniseya was a [[Force-sensitive]] witch who could wield [[the Force]]. Regarded by her as "the Thread," her [[Force power]]s included the ability to [[Telekinesis|move objects]], [[Force push|shove people around]], and to [[Force deflection|block Force attacks]]. To her, that her powers were dark was of no issue. During the ritual to initiate her daughters into being witches, she branded Mae with a mark of the coven, though she was interrupted before she could preform the rite on Osha. She was also able to weaponize the Thread by using an ability that would render an individual incapacitated and put them out of their right mind as their eyes turned fully black.<ref name="Destiny" />

Her psychic assault worked by in a mindscape standing before her victim and preying upon the target's fears. Additionally, she shifted into a smokey form and caused her daughter to seem disintegrate upon learning that her other child was in danger. In this form, she was still vulnerable to lightsabers and was killed by Sol when it seemed to him that she was unleashing another Force assault, this time on him and Mae.<ref name="Choice" /> The way she utilized the Force to fabricate life was seen by Sol as a very powerful skill,<ref name="Destiny AD" /> and the Jedi wondered if these matters of spontaneous-seeming life were boosted by a Force nexus at Aniseya's home.<ref name="Choice" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|In designing for Mother Aniseya and for the witches, I wanted to set them apart from what we've seen in previous ''Star Wars'' episodes and movies. I use purple as a color because it [evokes] a kind of royalty.|Jennifer Bryan, about the witches' Ascension costumes|<ref name="TurnerSmith">{{SW|url=news/the-acolyte-witches|text=In ''The Acolyte'', Jodie Turner-Smith's Mother Aniseya is Mothering}}</ref>}}
[[File:Jodie_Turner-Smith.jpg|thumb|right|230px|Jodie Turner-Smith, the actor who portrayed Mother Aniseya]]
Aniseya first appeared in "[[Destiny (The Acolyte)|Destiny]]," the third episode of the live-action [[Disney+]] series ''[[Star Wars: The Acolyte]]'',<ref name="Destiny" /> which aired on [[June 11]], [[2024]].<ref name="Press">{{DisneyPlus|subdomain=press|url=news/next-on-disney-plus-june-2024|text=Next on Disney+: June 2024}}</ref> In "Destiny," the character was portrayed by [[Jodie Turner-Smith]].<ref name="Getty">{{Getty|url=thewaltdisneystudios/allaccess#!asset/vrnhkzfjfz9j3q643rvkfgmt|text=The Walt Disney Studios All Access - PDX-FF-002650|date=2024-05-04}}</ref> Prior to the episode's release, she was first identified and visually depicted in both a [[StarWars.com]] in an article revealing information about some of the then-upcoming series's characters, which included Aniseya's coven of witches,<ref name="FirstLook">{{SW|url=news/the-acolyte-databank|text=''The Acolyte'' Characters Revealed — First Look}}</ref> and Aniseya's StarWars.com [[Databank (2014-)|Databank]] entry,<ref name="Databank-Aniseya">{{Databank|mother-aniseya|Mother Aniseya}}</ref> which were both released on [[March 18]], 2024. Her casting was also revealed in the article.<ref name="FirstLook" />

The robes Aniseya—and the rest of the coven's witches—wore during the Rite of Ascension were designed by ''The Acolyte''{{'s}} costume designer, [[Jennifer Bryan]]. Bryan indicated that the original color of the fabric upon arrival was more similar to a fuschia shade and had to be dyed to the royal purple seen in the finished episode.<ref name="Destiny Trivia">{{SW|url=destiny-trivia-gallery-the-acolyte|text="Destiny" Trivia Gallery | The Acolyte}} {{C|Slide 2}}</ref> The color purple for the costumes was chosen because purple evokes a feeling of royalty, and Bryan wished to reflect that the women in the episode were a group of elevated ladies. Mother Aniseya's costumes especially were meant to show her as a queen, elevated even above the other witches in quality of fabric.<ref name="TurnerSmith" />

In "Destiny," Aniseya and Koril are depicted as a caring pair of mothers<ref name="Destiny" /> who share several affectionate physical interactions.<ref name="Destiny AD">{{Acolyte|Destiny (The Acolyte)}} {{AD|Disney+}}</ref> ''The Acolyte''{{'s}} showrunner, [[Leslye Headland]], later indicated that she knew the pair's relationship had closeness between them seemed natural and plot driven. The showrunner also stated that while she knew their relationship would read that their sexuality was [[Wikipedia:Queer|queer]], that there also were not any men in their community, and noted that it would be "really reductive to call them lesbians." However, the creator also felt that if any her content was seen as queer, she was proud elements viewed as such by fans could inspire people.<ref name="Newsnet" />
